text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
- Large international investors are on a buying-spree of Nordic currencies, boosting them against the German mark.
- Finland's inspection of food products is spread between various authorities; trade sector wants centralisation.
- Travelling Finns are misers but too soft, survey shows. The price of travel is the main consideration and Finns demand too little and do not complain.
- National mediator Jorma Reini today in court charged with violence and resisting police. The government also plans to sack him today.
- Smoking increases face wrinkles and thins skin, studies show.
- Helsinki City sells 3,200 square metre city centre building site to Swedish construction group Skanska for 84 million markka for a hotel, or 105 million for an office block.
- Finland's Office for Free Competition grants two-year approval for current wood purchase price system, based on company-specific talks.

- Personal computer sales in Finland slowed clearly in 1996. However, IBM boosted sales by 70 percent to restore its position as market leader. Fujitsu-ICL was second and 1995 leader Compaq fell to third position.
- Nordic brewers have still not reached new production and distribution agreements with Coca-Cola.

- Finland's Swedish People's Party chairman Ole Norrback has wide support with 90 percent of key party officials behind him, survey shows. Second is Eva Biaudet who is now chairman of the parliamentary group.
- Proposal to raise value-added-tax has support in industry but medium and small size companies are against.
- Passport control at Finland's borders to be transferred to border guards from police.
